options: Петушки
Петушков
Петушкам
Петушках
cases.translation: What strangely tall houses they have put up in Petushki!
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (location, not direction) takes the prepositional; Петушки is a plural place name, so the ending is -ах.

cases.sentence: Я отошел от ___ и переводил свой тяжелый взгляд с дома на дом.
options: двери
дверей
дверям
дверями
cases.translation: I stepped away from the doors and moved my heavy gaze from house to house.
cases.explain: The preposition «от» (away from) always governs the genitive; here the noun is plural, giving дверей.

cases.sentence: Я свернул в ___, и снова задрожал и заплакал.
options: переулок
переулка
переулке
переулком
cases.translation: I turned into a side street, and started shivering and crying again.
cases.explain: «В» with motion (turning INTO somewhere) takes the accusative; переулок is inanimate, so its accusative matches the nominative.

cases.sentence: Орехов двести грамм, я ___ их вез.
options: младенец
младенца
младенцу
младенцем
cases.translation: Two hundred grams of nuts — I was bringing them to the little child.
cases.explain: The recipient of the verb «везти» (to bring something to someone) is the indirect object and stands in the dative: младенцу.

cases.sentence: И апостол предал Христа, покуда третий ___ не пропел.
options: петух
петуха
петуху
петухом
cases.translation: And the apostle betrayed Christ before the third cock had crowed.
cases.explain: The word is the subject of the verb «не пропел», and subjects stand in the nominative even when the verb is negated.

cases.sentence: Он еще грелся у ___, вместе с этими.
options: костёр
костра
костру
костром
cases.translation: He was still warming himself by the fire, together with that lot.
cases.explain: «У» meaning 'beside / at' governs the genitive; the ё of костёр drops out in the oblique forms, giving костра.

cases.sentence: Я задрожал сильнее прежнего, я весь превратился в сплошную ___.
options: судорога
судороги
судорогу
судорогой
cases.translation: I shook harder than before, I turned into one continuous convulsion.
cases.explain: «Превратиться в» (to turn into) takes «в» + accusative, so судорога becomes судорогу after the accusative adjective сплошную.

cases.sentence: Один ударил меня по щеке, другой – ___ в лицо.
options: кулак
кулака
кулаку
кулаком
cases.translation: One hit me on the cheek, another with his fist in the face.
cases.explain: The instrument used to perform an action stands in the instrumental case with no preposition: ударить кулаком.

reading.ru: Постучался – и, вздрагивая от холода, стал ждать, пока мне отворят…
reading.question: How does the chapter open?
options: He knocks and waits, shivering with cold, for someone to open the door
He is already sitting inside a warm room
He is buying vodka at a kiosk
He is asleep on a train to Petushki
reading.correct: He knocks and waits, shivering with cold, for someone to open the door
reading.explain: The first line has Venichka knocking and waiting in the cold for the door to be opened.

reading.ru: Странно высокие дома понастроили в Петушках!..
reading.question: What does Venichka say about the houses in Petushki?
options: That strangely tall houses have been built there
That they are all low wooden huts
That they have all been pulled down
That they are exactly like the ones in Moscow
reading.correct: That strangely tall houses have been built there
reading.explain: He is puzzled by the strangely tall houses, and blames it on his heavy hangover — everything looks bigger.

reading.ru: Они, серьезные, это понимают, а я, легковесный, никогда не пойму…
reading.question: How does Venichka contrast himself with other people here?
options: They are serious and understand, while he is lightweight and never will
They are lightweight while he alone is serious
Neither he nor they understand anything
He understands everything and they understand nothing
reading.correct: They are serious and understand, while he is lightweight and never will
reading.explain: He calls the others «серьезные» and himself «легковесный», picking up the Belshazzar phrase about being weighed and found wanting.

reading.ru: Я много прожил, много перепил и продумал – и знаю, что говорю.
reading.question: What does Venichka offer as his authority for what he is saying?
options: That he has lived much, drunk much and thought much
That he has read it in the newspapers
That a black-moustached man taught him
That the four strangers told him so
reading.correct: That he has lived much, drunk much and thought much
reading.explain: He backs his claim about the scales with his own experience of living, drinking and thinking things through.

reading.ru: Все ваши путеводные звезды катятся к закату, а если и не катятся, то едва мерцают.
reading.question: What does Venichka say about other people's guiding stars?
options: They are rolling towards sunset, or at best barely flickering
They shine brighter every year
They have already gone out completely
They are all the star of Bethlehem
reading.correct: They are rolling towards sunset, or at best barely flickering
reading.explain: He says every guiding star but one is setting or barely glimmering, which is why he cares only whether the star of Bethlehem is flaring up again.

reading.ru: Есть там весы, нет там весов – там мы, легковесные, перевесим и одолеем.
reading.question: What does Venichka predict about the 'lightweight' people like himself?
options: Scales or no scales, they will outweigh and prevail
They will be weighed and thrown away
They will never be weighed at all
They will become serious in the end
reading.correct: Scales or no scales, they will outweigh and prevail
reading.explain: Whether or not the scales exist, he insists the lightweight ones will tip the balance and win.

reading.ru: Но почему же так странно расширили улицы в Петушках?..
reading.question: What question does Venichka keep coming back to during his speech?
options: Why the streets in Petushki have been made so strangely wide
Why the shops in Petushki are shut
Why nobody in Petushki knows his name
Why the train to Petushki was late
reading.correct: Why the streets in Petushki have been made so strangely wide
reading.explain: His prophetic speech breaks off twice with bewilderment at the size of the buildings and the width of the streets.

reading.ru: Если б у меня было хоть двадцать глотков кубанской!
reading.question: What does Venichka wish he had at this moment?
options: At least twenty swallows of Kubanskaya vodka
A glass of coriander vodka
A mug of Zhiguli beer
A cup of hot tea
reading.correct: At least twenty swallows of Kubanskaya vodka
reading.explain: He believes twenty gulps of Kubanskaya would reach his heart, and his heart would then convince his reason that he really is in Petushki.

reading.ru: Но кубанской не было: я свернул в переулок, и снова задрожал и заплакал…
reading.question: What does Venichka do when it turns out there is no Kubanskaya?
options: He turns into a side street and starts shivering and crying again
He goes back and knocks at the door once more
He lies down on the pavement and falls asleep
He runs straight to the station
reading.correct: He turns into a side street and starts shivering and crying again
reading.explain: With no vodka to steady him he turns off into a lane, trembling and in tears — and that is where the four are waiting.

reading.ru: Я сразу их узнал, я не буду вам объяснять, кто эти четверо…
reading.question: What does Venichka say about the four men who come towards him?
options: He recognised them at once and will not explain to us who they are
He had never seen anyone like them before
They were old drinking companions of his
They were railway workers from Petushki
reading.correct: He recognised them at once and will not explain to us who they are
reading.explain: He refuses to name them, saying only that he knew them immediately.

reading.ru: А они подошли и меня обступили.
reading.question: What do the four do when they reach Venichka?
options: They come up and surround him
They walk straight past him
They ask him for money
They run away from him
reading.correct: They come up and surround him
reading.explain: They close in around him, and he then tries to describe their faces and their eyes.

reading.ru: Ну, вот ты и попался, – сказал один.
reading.question: What is the first thing one of the four says to Venichka?
options: That he has finally been caught
That he must pay them six roubles
That the train to Petushki has left
That they will show him the way to the Kremlin
reading.correct: That he has finally been caught
reading.explain: The exchange opens with «Ну, вот ты и попался» and the flat announcement that he will not be going anywhere else.

reading.ru: Я знаю, почему он предал, – потому что дрожал от холода, да.
reading.question: Why, according to Venichka, did the apostle betray Christ?
options: Because he was shivering with cold
Because he had been paid to do it
Because he did not recognise him
Because he had been drinking all night
reading.correct: Because he was shivering with cold
reading.explain: Venichka argues nobody can be sure of himself on a cold night, and adds that the apostle at least had a fire to warm himself at.

reading.ru: Какой еще василек? – со злобою спросил один.
reading.question: How does one of the four react when Venichka mentions «Василек»?
options: He asks spitefully what sort of cornflower that is supposed to be
He laughs and offers Venichka a sweet
He says he knows the shop where they are sold
He says nothing at all
reading.correct: He asks spitefully what sort of cornflower that is supposed to be
reading.explain: Venichka has to explain that «Василек» is the name of the sweets he was carrying in the stolen suitcase.

reading.ru: Не поедешь ты ни в какие Петушки!
reading.question: What do the four tell Venichka when he says he wants to go to Petushki again?
options: That he is not going to any Petushki
That the last train has already gone
That they will take him there themselves
That he should go to the Kremlin instead
reading.correct: That he is not going to any Petushki
reading.explain: They refuse him Petushki, and then refuse him the Kursk station as well.

reading.ru: Я схватился за голову – и побежал.
reading.question: How does the chapter end?
options: He clutches his head and runs, with the four right behind him
He falls down and loses consciousness
He drives the four men off
He walks calmly away and boards a train
reading.correct: He clutches his head and runs, with the four right behind him
reading.explain: After being struck he takes his own advice to run anywhere at all, and the four set off after him.

highlight.question: Which sentence quotes the words of the writing on the wall and translates them?
sentences: Я еще раз постучался, чуть громче прежнего: «Неужели так трудно отворить человеку дверь и впустить его на три минуты погреться?
Я этого не понимаю…
Они, серьезные, это понимают, а я, легковесный, никогда не пойму…
Мене, текел, фарес – то есть „ты взвешен на весах и найден легковесным“, то есть „текел“…
Ну и пусть, пусть…
highlight.explain: The fourth sentence gives the Belshazzar formula and glosses it as being weighed and found wanting.

highlight.question: Which sentence says what will outweigh calculation and design on those scales?
sentences: Но есть ли там весы или нет – все равно – на тех весах вздох и слеза перевесят расчет и умысел.
Я это знаю тверже, чем вы что-нибудь знаете.
Я много прожил, много перепил и продумал – и знаю, что говорю.
Все ваши путеводные звезды катятся к закату, а если и не катятся, то едва мерцают.
highlight.explain: The first sentence names the sigh and the tear as what tips the balance against calculation and intent.

highlight.question: Which sentence breaks off the prophecy with a question about the streets of Petushki?
sentences: Есть там весы, нет там весов – там мы, легковесные, перевесим и одолеем.
Я прочнее в это верю, чем вы во что-нибудь верите.
Верю, и знаю, и свидетельствую миру.
Но почему же так странно расширили улицы в Петушках?..
highlight.explain: The paragraph of prophecy ends abruptly with his bewilderment at the widened streets.

highlight.question: Which sentence says what Venichka actually did once there turned out to be no vodka?
sentences: Если б у меня было хоть двадцать глотков кубанской!
Они подошли бы к сердцу, и сердце всегда сумело бы убедить рассудок, что я в Петушках!
Но кубанской не было: я свернул в переулок, и снова задрожал и заплакал…
highlight.explain: The first two sentences are a wish and its imagined effect; only the third reports what he did.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that Venichka knew the four men immediately but refuses to say who they are?
sentences: И тут – началась история, страшнее всех, виденных во сне: в этом самом переулке навстречу мне шли четверо…
Я сразу их узнал, я не буду вам объяснять, кто эти четверо…
Я задрожал сильнее прежнего, я весь превратился в сплошную судорогу…
highlight.explain: The second sentence combines instant recognition with his refusal to explain.

highlight.question: Which sentence shows Venichka trying to remember where he had seen those faces before?
sentences: Все четверо смотрели на меня в упор, и все четверо, наверно, думали: «Как этот подонок труслив и элементарен!»
О, пусть, пусть себе думают, только бы отпустили!..
Где, в каких газетах я видел эти рожи?..
highlight.explain: The last sentence asks in which newspapers he had seen those mugs before.
